changes: Fourth-batch source-reviewed publication. Cross-verified from official 0.5 patch notes, current creator guides, an independent build guide, a planner, a current gameplay video and community questions.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This Infernalist progresses from Level 1: you level with Spark, add Frostbolt, then enable Cast on Critical (CoC) with Comet once the trigger tools exist. Recoup and Ward are layered on top for defense and a high-end variant.
Verification-first: the exact progression overlaps and variant math come from the current creator guide. The trigger diagnostic and the 'Ward is a variant' framing are the actionable core.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Smooth Level 1 to endgame path with clear stages.
Recoup turns the Infernalist downside into a defense.
Ward variant exists for players who want it.
cons: Complex trigger interactions; not a beginner build.
Comet may not trigger if crit/energy/socket rules are wrong.
Ward is not invincibility; uptime matters.
Final Form needs a budget the starter does not have.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick this if you want a caster that scales from league start into a trigger-based endgame and you are comfortable with CoC setup. It is not a copy-paste Final Form on day one.
Start with Spark and follow the stage gates; do not jump to the final CoC from Level 1.

steps.label: Campaign - Spark
body: Level with Spark. It is the safe campaign clearer before Frostbolt and CoC.

steps.label: Early Frostbolt
body: Add Frostbolt once available; still pre-trigger.

steps.label: CoC available
body: Enable Cast on Critical with Comet once the trigger link and crit exist.

steps.label: Cheap Endgame

steps.label: Ward Stacking / Final Form
body: High-investment variants only after the cheap endgame is comfortable.

sections.title: Trigger Mechanics
paragraphs: Cast on Critical spends trigger energy on critical hits and automatically casts the linked Comet. Energy is generated by crits, so critical chance and cast speed are the limiter - not raw spell damage.

sections.title: Recoup Mechanics
paragraphs: Recoup returns a portion of damage taken as life/ES over time. It solves the Infernalist's self-damage downside and sustains mapping, but it does not cover every burst - a huge one-shot still kills.

sections.title: Ward Variant
paragraphs: Ward stacking is a high-end variant, not the default. It inverts some resource rules and is likely 0.5-specific; treat it as an optional branch, not the league-start loadout.

whyUse: The main single-target and clear engine once online.

recommendations: An ES base with recoup and resistances. The defensive anchor.
Spell level, crit, cast speed. Upgrade priority for damage.
Ward-converting gear only for the high-end variant.

steps.label: Starter -> Cheap Endgame
body: Cap resistances, secure recoup and ES, enable CoC.

steps.label: Cheap -> Expensive
body: Add crit and cast speed; raise spell level.

steps.label: Expensive -> Ward/Final
body: Only after cheap endgame is comfortable; high-investment branch.

sections.title: Budget Variants
paragraphs: Cheap Endgame is the realistic league-start target. Expensive adds crit. Ward Stacking and Final Form are high-investment branches - Final Form is not a low-budget build.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Recoup plus Energy Shield is the core. Ward adds a layer in the variant but is not invincibility; keep resistances capped and watch for one-shots that bypass recoup.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: For mapping: keep Spark/Frostbolt feeding CoC, maintain recoup uptime, and move. The clear is automatic once the trigger is tuned.

sections.title: Rare Rotation
paragraphs: For rares: ensure crit/energy so Comet fires; if it stalls, check the single-target config rather than dumping more damage gems.

sections.title: Boss Rotation
paragraphs: For bosses: pre-cast setup, let CoC do the work, and manage mana/recoup during the fight. Do not expect the Final Form numbers on a starter budget.

sections.title: Community Voices

entries.label: Reddit - CoC mana

entries.label: Forum - Ward stacking
entries.statement: Many assume Ward equals invincible; experienced players clarify uptime and other defense still matter.

entries.label: Guide comments - when to swap
entries.statement: New players ask when to leave Spark; the guide recommends a clear stage gate rather than a fixed level.

sections.note: Short paraphrases of common community questions and concerns, edited for clarity. Not verbatim quotes.

items.question: Why do leveling stages overlap?
answer: Because skills like Spark persist into early maps while Frostbolt/CoC are being introduced. Overlap is intentional; follow the stage gates, not a single level.

items.question: What does Recoup actually solve?
answer: It returns a portion of damage taken as life/ES over time, sustaining the Infernalist self-damage and mapping. It does not cover every burst.

items.question: Why is Ward not the default?
answer: Ward stacking inverts resource rules and is a high-investment variant, likely 0.5-specific. The league-start loadout is the recoup endgame.

items.question: Why does copying Final Form fail for new players?
answer: Final Form needs crit gear, Ward conversion and a budget the starter lacks. Build the cheap endgame first, then branch.
